questions.stem: What does dynamic data masking do in a Fabric warehouse?

options.text: It encrypts the column's values on disk, so they can be read only by users holding the decryption key
It hides a column's values in query results for users without the UNMASK permission; the stored data doesn't change
It removes the column from the table and stores its values in a separate secured table that only UNMASK users can read
It blocks every query on the table for users without the UNMASK permission until an admin approves

questions.explanation: Masking changes what non-privileged users see in results. The data itself is stored unchanged.

questions.stem: Which three are dynamic data masking functions? Each correct answer is a complete solution.
questions.explanation: Masking functions include default(), email(), random() and partial(). Encryption and hashing aren't masking functions.

questions.stem: At Harbor Health, one compliance officer among the analysts must see real email addresses. What do you do, with the least privilege?

options.text: Remove the mask from the column for everyone
Copy the table without the mask for them
Grant the UNMASK permission to the compliance officer
Make the compliance officer a workspace Admin

questions.explanation: UNMASK lets a user see the real values while the mask stays in place for everyone else. Making the officer a workspace Admin would also unmask the data, but it gives far more access than needed.

questions.stem: Which statement about dynamic data masking is true?

options.text: It applies to workspace Admins, Members and Contributors too, so no workspace role can ever see the unmasked values
It makes masked values impossible to infer, because filters such as WHERE or LIKE on a masked column are always blocked
It replaces the need for row-level security, because rows with masked values are also filtered out of query results for non-privileged users
It isn't a complete security boundary: a user who can query a column can still infer values with filters, so combine it with permissions

questions.explanation: Masking limits exposure in results, but a user with SELECT can run queries such as WHERE Email LIKE 'a%' to learn about values. Use it alongside column and row permissions.

questions.stem: A Salary column is masked. An engineer with the Contributor workspace role queries it and sees real salaries. Why?

options.text: Masks apply only to queries that come from Power BI reports, not from T-SQL
The mask was applied with the default() function instead of the partial() function
Admin, Member and Contributor roles have CONTROL on the database, which includes UNMASK
Contributors see masked values only when querying the table through the SQL analytics endpoint

questions.explanation: Workspace Admins, Members and Contributors have CONTROL on the database by design, and CONTROL includes UNMASK, so they see unmasked data.

questions.stem: An Email column is masked with email(). What does a user without UNMASK see for the value john.smith@contoso.net?
questions.explanation: email() exposes the first letter and the constant suffix .com in the form of an email address.

questions.stem: A Phone column is masked with partial(1,"XXXXXXX",0). What does a user without UNMASK see for 555.123.1234?
questions.explanation: partial() keeps the given number of leading and trailing characters and puts the padding in between. With a prefix of 1 and a suffix of 0, only the first character remains.

questions.stem: A security officer must add a mask to an existing column in a warehouse table. Which two permissions does this require? Each correct answer is part of the solution.
questions.explanation: Adding, replacing or removing a mask needs ALTER ANY MASK and ALTER on the table. UNMASK lets you see real values, and ALTER ANY SECURITY POLICY is for row-level security.

questions.stem: A BirthDate column of type date is masked with default(). What do users without UNMASK see?

options.text: A random date in the same year

questions.explanation: default() masks by data type: strings become XXXX, numbers become zero, and date and time values become 1900-01-01 00:00:00.0000000.

questions.stem: A numeric Month column must show users a random value from 1 to 12 instead of the real month. Which statement do you run?
questions.explanation: random() replaces a numeric value with a random value in the range you give. default() would show zero, and partial() is for strings.
